name: ascii-art
title: ASCII Art Renderer
description: Turns an image into a grid of text characters whose density follows brightness. A panel can animate in with a green matrix sweep, a fade or a typewriter, leaving a character-drawn picture.
use: A tech or portfolio page wants an image rendered as text that decodes itself on scroll.
avoid: The glyphs are decorative and unreadable as text, and the source image must be readable without CORS errors.
a11y: The canvas has an image role and label, but the label only says it is ASCII art, not what the picture shows. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Two side-by-side ASCII panels on a near-black stage: on the left the outline of a dog built from dense grey characters, on the right palm trees drawn as pale block glyphs. Small grey captions sit below each panel.
behaves: Each picture is redrawn from character density rather than pixels. On entering view a green diagonal band sweeps the left panel, showing glowing random glyphs ahead of the front until the whole image is legible, then it holds still.
customise: Set the source image, character resolution, charset preset or custom string, colour or coloured mode, animation style and timing, font and fit.
weight: moderate: Draws thousands of glyphs to a canvas during the reveal, then holds a still frame.
demo: A dog drawn in characters beside a palm-tree scene in blocks, captioned "matrix reveal" and "colored blocks".
issues: The canvas label says only that it is ASCII art, not what image it shows.
Thin characters merge into noise at small panel sizes, so the picture only reads large.
polishWhy: Sharp character rendering and a striking green sweep; the pictures blur into noise when small.
